items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: Teal was probably the greatest of the Teal. He laid out in the style.

ctx.x: In a sense I think that those clarinet players, Barney and Noon especially, were part of a family. In other words they were not especially creators even though they had great originality and you identify them immediately. They're of a family, maybe comes back from Teal. Teal and Bache.

Teal was probably the greatest of the Teal. He laid out in the style. Then Bache came along before he took up that old soprano sax. I never could see why Bache took that dog on soprano sax. Yet he made a whole lot of money with it. Well see people don't, they're lame like that's paying the bills, they don't know anything about what's going on.

Well actually it may have been the same sense of novelty that you noticed when you started off with an alto. It was a novel thing. Well it caught on to where it became a conventional instrument. Maybe the soprano could have become a conventional instrument instead of a bastard instrument but it has remained.
